title: She didn’t break the command.
paragraphs:
She didn’t break the command.
She added to it.
And that was enough to break everything.

Not at the fruit.
Not at the serpent.

Because buried in Eve’s words…
is the seed of every distortion you and I still believe today.

God said:
“You shall not eat of the tree…” (Genesis 2:17)

Eve said:
“You shall not eat… nor shall you touch it…” (Genesis 3:3)

One extra line.
One small exaggeration.

God feels stricter than He is.
Closer to a tyrant than a Father.
More about restriction than relationship.

Because when God feels unreasonable…
sin starts to look reasonable.

When God feels harsh…
disobedience starts to feel justified.

And just like that—
truth doesn’t need to be denied…

The first deception in human history
didn’t begin with rebellion.
It began with a misrepresentation of God’s Word.
“I’ve messed up too much… God won’t take me back.”

Both feel real.
Both sound convincing.

Some of us make God softer than He is—
to excuse our sin.

Others make God harsher than He is—
to excuse our shame.
But both roads lead to the same place:

He is already perfectly holy.
Perfectly just.
Perfectly good.

When you add to His Word,
you don’t protect His holiness—

Because once you believe a false version of God,
you will respond to Him incorrectly.
“Do not add to His words, lest He rebuke you and you be found a liar.” — Proverbs 30:6

That’s not just a command.
That’s protection.

Because adding to God’s Word
creates a god who doesn’t exist.
And a false god can’t save you.
Now here’s where it gets deeper.
The serpent didn’t start with a lie.

Because once truth is slightly bent,
it becomes easier to fully break.
Where have you added to what God said?

Where have you made Him stricter…
or softer…
than He actually is?

Where have you rewritten His voice
to match your fear… or your desire?

That “but” has destroyed more lives
than open defiance ever did.
Because the story didn’t end in a garden.

Where Eve distorted God’s Word…
Jesus defended it perfectly.

When Satan tempted Him, Jesus didn’t add.
He didn’t twist.
He didn’t soften.

And where Adam and Eve fell through distortion—
Jesus stood in truth.

Because perfect obedience alone
wasn’t enough to save you.

He carried every lie you believed.
Every distortion you accepted.
Every moment you edited God
to justify sin or magnify shame.
“For our sake He made Him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.” — 2 Corinthians 5:21

But full redemption
through Jesus Christ alone.
Your problem is not just that you’ve sinned.
Your problem is that you’ve believed lies about God.
And your solution is not trying harder.

Your solution is seeing Him rightly—
through Jesus.
Because Jesus is not an edited version of God.
“The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His being…” — Hebrews 1:3

If you want to know what God is like—
look at Christ.

Not your fear.
Not your feelings.
Not your assumptions.
Come back to what God actually said.

Not what culture says.
Not what trauma whispers.
Not what your guilt screams.

And if you’ve been running—
because you thought God was too harsh…

He is holy, yes.
But He is also merciful.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us…” — 1 John 1:9

And if you’ve been hiding—
because you made God too soft…

Grace is not permission to stay in sin.
It’s power to be free from it.
“Shall we continue in sin that grace may abound? By no means!” — Romans 6:1–2

Not just from sin—
but from believing a distorted God.
Say it if you mean it:

“Jesus, I surrender what I thought You were.
Show me who You truly are.”
If this exposed something in you…

From distortion to truth.
From shame to redemption.
Because Jesus doesn’t just correct your words—
